key_insight: StateDRIFT tailors Hamiltonian-term sampling to the initial state and target observable, reducing estimation bias and variance while retaining qDRIFT’s guarantees through a provable truncation bound.
engineering_relevance: Lower-depth simulations can reduce two-qubit gate requirements for estimating quantum dynamics at a target accuracy.
method: Optimise sampling probabilities at each circuit depth to target bias and/or variance.
Use initial-state observables and commutators to inform the distribution.
Estimate required quantities with classical surrogates, such as tensor networks, or classical shadows.
evidence_signal: Tests on short-time lattice and molecular dynamics up to 18 qubits included a BeH2 example reducing two-qubit gates from 11,201 to 983 at a given accuracy.
watch_item: Practical savings depend on the cost and accuracy of estimating initial-state quantities; performance beyond the tested short-time regimes remains to be established.
paper_title: Problem-aware sampling for bias and variance reduction in randomised Hamiltonian simulation
